newsitem.title: FRANCE: Globalstar partner sees 1999 start in satellite service.
newsitem.headline: Globalstar partner sees 1999 start in satellite service.

text.p: Globalstar, a satellite-based communications system designed to enable customers to make phone calls, transmit data and faxes on the go in more than 100 countries, will begin service on Jan. 1, 1999, an official with one of the project's partners and suppliers said Wednesday.
Alcatel Espace Chairman Jean-Claude Husson also told reporters that financing for Globalstar -- a San Jose, Calif.-based international effort expected to cost $2.5 billion -- was nearly all in place.

Globalstar will make a variety of global communications possible via a network of 48 satellites in low orbit plus eight back-up satellites. The satellites are to be put in orbit by September 1998, Husson said.
The system will break even when it has around 2.5 million users, he said.
Globalstar LP was founded by New York-based Loral Corp. and San Diego-based Qualcomm Inc.
Alcatel Espace is a unit of French electrical engineering company Alcatel Alsthom.
Globalstar is designed to allow paging as well as phone calls, data transmission and faxes via hand-held, vehicle-mounted or fixed terminals.
